stem: Many copper compounds, such as $\text{CuSO}_4$ and $\text{Cu(NO}_3\text{)}_2$ contain $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ions. Aqueous solutions of this ion contain the $[\text{Cu(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ complex ion, in which water behaves as a monodentate ligand.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term *monodentate ligand*.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Copper(II) sulfate solution, $\text{CuSO}_4\text{(aq)}$, undergoes visible changes with certain reagents.

Complete the table below.

| reagent added to a solution of $\text{CuSO}_4\text{(aq)}$ | observations | formula of the copper(II) compound or complex ion that is formed |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| a few drops of $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$ |  |  |
| an excess of $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$ |  |  |
| an excess of $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ |  |  |
| an excess of concentrated $\text{HCl(aq)}$ |  |  |

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
When water is added to concentrated aqueous cobalt(II) chloride the colour of the solution changes from blue to pink. Explain this observation.

No equation is needed, but you should include reference to electron movement between orbitals in your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
When chlorine gas is bubbled into $\text{FeSO}_4\text{(aq)}$ the colour of the solution changes from pale green to yellow.

Use data from the *Data Booklet* to explain this observation. Include an equation in your answer.

Reference to electron movement between orbitals is not needed.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
If a solution of chloride ions is added to a solution containing $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ an equilibrium is established.

$$[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+} + 4\text{Cl}^- \rightleftharpoons [\text{FeCl}_4]^- + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
parts.text: Write an expression for the stability constant of $[\text{FeCl}_4]^-$, $K_{\text{stab}}$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
For the above equilibrium the numerical value of $K_{\text{stab}} = 0.080$.

Calculate the concentration of $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ in a solution in which the concentration of $\text{Cl}^-$ is $2.0\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ and the concentration of $[\text{FeCl}_4]^-$ is $0.10\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.
